title: The role of externally-driven density fluctuations in the enhancement of beam spray
byline: McMillen; Kyle R; Min-Roberts; Ian D; Follett; Russell K; Milder; Avram L; Katz; Joseph; Haberberger; Daniel J; Gordillo; Julieta Hernandez; Michel; Pierre A; R
html:
Abstract:Speckled laser beams, commonly used to ionize and heat plasma for inertial confinement fusion and high-energy-density experiments, are shown to drive long-wavelength plasma-density fluctuations that induce beam spray in other laser beams. Experiments show that a 1053 nm beam undergoes increased beam spray when 351 nm speckled heater beams are on. These observations indicate that the high-intensity speckles sustain an increased level of steady-state density fluctuations. Modeling of these fluctuations predicts amplitudes that are orders of magnitude larger than the level of thermal fluctuations. Beam propagation simulations show increased beam spray due to self-focusing and filamentation when heater-driven density fluctuations are included.
